descriptionChirho: The human voice as the instrument of speech, crying, singing, or any vocal utterance — includes possessive inflections (my voice, his voice, your voice, their voice, her voice, our voice) and all prepositional forms (to/with/in the voice of) — Arabic صَوْت (vocal), Korean 목소리/음성/소리, Swahili sauti, Hindi आवाज़/स्वर.

The voice of the LORD (קוֹל יהוה), the voice of God speaking in revelation, command, or theophany — a distinctly theological use where the voice carries divine authority and demands obedience (שׁמע בְּקוֹל = obey the voice of); frequently in construct with divine names — Arabic صَوْتُ الرَّبِّ, Korean (하나님의) 음성, Swahili sauti ya Bwana, Hindi यहोवा की आवाज़.

An audible sound, noise, or acoustic phenomenon not produced by a human or divine voice — the sound of water, wind, chariots, trumpets, wings, millstones, battle, or other non-vocal sources — Arabic صَوْت (of things), Korean 소리, Swahili sauti, Hindi ध्वनि/आवाज़.

Thunder, thunderclaps — the plural קוֹלוֹת used for peals of thunder, often in theophanic or storm contexts (Exodus 9, 19–20; Psalm 29); metaphorically 'the voice of God' as thunder — Arabic رُعُود, Korean 천둥/천둥들, Swahili ngurumo, Hindi गड़गड़ाहटें/गरज.
A report, rumor, fame, or tidings — what is heard and passed on; the content of what is spoken rather than the act of speaking — Arabic خَبَر (news), Korean 소식/소문, Swahili habari/sauti, Hindi ख़बर.

The voice as the object of obedience in the idiom שׁמע בְּקוֹל (hear/heed the voice of) — a specialized collocational sense where 'voice' stands for authority, command, or instruction to be obeyed — Arabic لِصَوْتِ (with سمع), Korean 음성을 (듣다), Swahili sauti (kusikia), Hindi आवाज़ (सुनना/मानना).
